_doc: EXAMPLE ONLY, AND INACTIVE. Adds focused scopes to bench's own
verify/ entrypoints so a run can check what it touched before it
asks for the whole suite. Nothing reads this file: it changes no grant,
gate or prompt until an operator reviews it and applies it through
Settings (validate, preview, apply) or copies the parts they want into
manager/local/profiles.json by hand.
A focused selection is a SCOPE of the full check, never a check of its
own name and never part of the check's `run`. That is what keeps it
honest: bench binds a scope's arguments into the check's coverage and
result identity, so `bench-backend contracts` passing does not answer a
requirement for `bench-backend`, is not reused for a full request, and
reads stale when its selection changes. The bare name is still the
whole suite. This document declares NO gates block: a merge rule, if
you want one, requires the bare name (the full run), never a focused
scope, and adding it is a separate decision in Settings → Merge rules.
Scopes name modules and cases explicitly. None is inferred from changed
files: choosing what to check early is the run's judgement, and the
full run at the final commit is still the evidence a merge reads.
bench-browser's scopes run over whichever transport the machine has;
on the devbox that is the remote Playwright server PW_WS names
(verify/README.md, 'Remote Playwright'). A case using an API only one
transport has is refused before the browser starts, focused or not.
